plan: My value is $35. In a second-price auction, bidding my true value is generally optimal to maximize profit. Since this is the first round and there's no history, I will bid my true value to establish a baseline and see how other bidders behave. This strategy aims to secure the item if the winning price is below my value, maximizing my profit in the long run.

I will bid slightly below my value to maximize profit while still having a good chance to win. Since the payment is the second-highest bid, bidding my full value might lead to paying my full value if the second-highest bid is also high. Bidding slightly below my value (e.g., 90-95% of my value) offers a good balance. I will bid 30.

My value is 48. In this auction, the winner pays the second-highest bid. To maximize profit, I want to win when the second-highest bid is as low as possible, but still win against other bidders. Since values are drawn between 0 and 49, and I have a high value, I should bid high. A bid of 47.9 seems reasonable to try to win against most bids while leaving some profit margin.
